news.title: Flamingos receive big cash reward after winning FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Find it fast with our new search feature at Legit.ng! Nigeria's Flamingos have received a $50,000 cash reward after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Rabat, Morocco, becoming the first African nation to win the tournament. The gift was presented by Alhaji Saleh Ahmadu, a sponsor of the National Sports Commission, at a reception held in Rabat on Saturday night in honour of the victorious squad. National Sports Commission Chairman Shehu Dikko and Director-General Bukola Olopade hosted the event, which was also attended by the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi.

news.title: Flamingos Coach Hakeem Busari Celebrates Historic FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Victory
news.lede: Hakeem Busari, head coach of the Nigerian national under-17 women's football team known as the Flamingos, has publicly commended his players for their exceptional resilience and tactical discipline. This praise follows the team's historic campaign at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, where they secured the first-ever continental triumph for an African nation. Busari emphasized that the victory was not accidental but the result of sustained development and strong character displayed by the squad throughout the tournament. Historic Victory Over JapanThe Flamingos achieved a landmark moment in African sports history by defeating the Japanese national team in the final match.

news.title: Flamingos’ World Cup Triumph Reinforces Need For Grassroots Football Development – Araba
news.lede: Femi Sanni (Araba), chairman, Stafolga Group/ Flow FM, proprietor of Araba Football Club and grassroots football development advocate, has described Nigeria’s historic victory at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup as a compelling demonstration of the importance of talent discovery, youth development and sustained investment in football. Araba, who congratulated the Flamingos and their Kwara-born head coach, Akeem Ishola Busari, after their 2–1 victory over Japan in Rabat, Morocco, said the achievement should inspire greater commitment to grassroots football across the country. Nigeria’s triumph marked the first time an African country had won the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

news.title: Nigeria 2-1 Japan: CAF reacts as Flamingos win FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark Legit.ng as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Nigeria's Flamingos have made history by becoming the first African women's team to win a FIFA competition, claiming the U-17 Women's World Cup title with a 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday's final at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat, Morocco. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring in the 39th minute, before Oluebube Umejiaku doubled the lead in the 47th minute. Japan's Fuki Ito pulled one back for the Little Nadeshiko, but the Flamingos held firm to secure the trophy.

news.title: Akinwunmi Hails Tinubu’s Sports Reforms As Flamingos Make World Cup History
news.lede: Former First Vice President of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) and former Chairman of the Lagos State Football Association, Seyi Akinwunmi, has commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s sports development agenda and the National Sports Commission (NSC), following Nigeria’s historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Akinwunmi spoke in Lagos shortly after the Flamingos defeated Japan in the final to become the first African nation to win the competition, describing the achievement as a landmark moment for Nigerian football and a validation of sustained investment in grassroots and youth development. He attributed the triumph partly to the Federal Government’s renewed attention to sports development, particularly the reforms being implemented by the NSC under the administration of President Tinubu. “This victory did not happen by chance,” he said.

news.title: Nigeria 2:1 Japan: FIFA Sends Message to Flamingos After Winning U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark Legit.ng as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Nigeria's Flamingos claimed the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title on Saturday, November 7, defeating Japan 2-1 in the final held at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat, Morocco, to write their names into the history books. The victory made Nigeria the first African country to lift the trophy in the history of the competition, capping off a remarkable tournament run that included a 3-1 semi-final win over Brazil. As seen on FIFA's official website, Nigeria took control of the match before half-time when Awawu Bashiru struck from distance in the 39th minute.

news.title: Argentina FA to appeal World Cup final sanctions to CAS
news.lede: Argentina’s football association (AFA) announced on Saturday it had appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the sanctions FIFA imposed on it over World Cup final incidents. Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the hardest hit with a 10-game ban and $90,000 fine for his role in clashes with Spain players. He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground while holding his substitute’s bib, which led to an escalation in the incidents on the field after the final that Spain won 1-0 at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19. The AFA was fined $321,000 for breaches of FIFA’s disciplinary code relating to using a sports event for making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discriminatory chants and gestures by its supporters.
